slides.title: Torch Cutting and Welding
slides.description:
Torch-cutting and welding operations can expose shop employees to many types of hazards to include the following:

  • Fumes
  • Electric shock
  • Radiation burns
  • Burns from hot metals
  • Temporary or permanent eye damage
  • Fire and explosion
  • Compressed gas

his section will give you many safety rules and tips for torches, regulators, hoses, connections and cylinders.

slides.title: Torches
slides.description:
• You must not use torches unless you are trained and authorized to do so.
  • Only torches approved by management are to be used.
  • Proper eye protection must be worn at all times. Safety glasses must be worn beneath cutting goggles.
  • Connections on a torch should be checked for tightness after assembly or on a regular basis (preferably daily)
  • A friction lighter must be used to ingnite a torch.
  • Torches must be designed for the gas that is going to be used.
  • Oxygen must never be used as a substitute for compressed air.
  • Oil, grease and other lubricants must be kept away from fittings, hoses, regulators, etc. They may cause explosions.
  • Before changing torches, shut off the gas at the pressure-reducing regulators. Do not crimp the hose to shut off the torch.

slides.title: Regulators
slides.description:
• Stand to one side, away from the regulator gauge when operating cylinder valves. Be sure cylinders are secure and in an upright position.
  • Regulators (oxygen or fuel gas) should be equipped with both a high-pressure tank (contents) gauge and low-pressure (working) gauge.
  • Never drop or pound on regulators.
  • Leaking regulators should be removed from service.
  • Connect the regulator to the outlet valve on the cylinder. Be sure the regulator inlet threads match the cylinder valve outlet threads. Never connect an oxygen regulator to a cylinder containing fuel gas or vise versa. Do not force connection that do not fit easily. Be sure connections between the regulators and cylinder valves are tight. Do not use an oil or lubricant on the threads of the connectors.
  • Release the pressure by adjusting the screw on the regulators to its limit and then turning the screw counterclockwise until it is loose.
  • Open the cylinder valve slightly to let the dial hand on the high-pressure gauge move up slowly. On an oxygen cylinder, gradually open the cylinder valve to its full limit. But, on an acetylene cylinder make no more than a half turn on the valve spindle.

slides.title: Regulators cont’d
slides.description:
• Attach oxygen hose to outlet of oxygen regulator and to oxygen inlet valve on torch. Attach acetylene hose to outlet of acetylene regulator and to acetylene inlet on torch.
  • Test oxygen connection for leaks by using soapy water. Be sure the oxygen valve on the torch is closed. Then turn the oxygen regulator pressure-adjusting screw clockwise to give normal working pressure. Test regulators for leak with soapy water.
  • To adjust the pressure of oxygen and fuel gas prior to using the torch, proceed with the following:
    • With all torch valves closed, slowly open oxygen cylinder valve.
    • Open torch oxygen valve
    • Turn on pressure-adjusting screw on oxygen regulator to desired pressure.
  • Purge each line individually. Open oxygen torch valve and release oxygen to atmosphere for a second or two before closing the valve. Then, open acetylene torch valve and release acetylene to the atmosphere for a second or two and close valves.
  • Open torch acetylene valve, light flame and adjust regulator.
  • Open the oxygen torch valves and adjust the torch according to procedures supplies by manufacturer.

slides.title: Hoses and Hose Connections
slides.description:
• The length of hoses should only be as long as necessary. Keep hoses from being linked or tangled
  • Keep hoses and lines away from walkways, steps, etc., so tripping hazards are not created.
  • Never tape a hose when it is leaking. The hose should be replaced.
  • Keep hoses away from sparks and flames. Do not operate a torch directly over a hose.
  • Reverse-flow check valves should be installed on the hose ends, preferably at the torch.
  • The condition of the hose reel and hose-real supports should be checked periodically for any maintenance problems or loose bolts.

slides.title: Cylinders
slides.description:
• Cylinders should be secured at all times while being transported.
  • If a fusible safety plug on an acetylene cylinder must be used, it will melt at boiling point of water.
  • Frozen outlet valves may be thawed with warm (not boiling) water.
  • Cylinders must be stored in a safe, dry, shaded and ventilated area. The floor of the storage area should be flat and fireproof.
  • Cylinders must be secured in an upright position. The cylinder cap must be tightly in place, unless the cylinder is equipped with gauges.
  • Cylinders should be secured on an individual basis and not chained together.
  • Oxygen and acetylene cylinders (and other flammable material) must be stored apart by 20 feet or more. If this isn’t possible, a partition must be placed between the cylinders. The partition must be 5 feet high and have a ½ hour fire rating.
  • The procedures covered in the previous slide onRegulatorsshould be followed when installing gauges.
  • If a cylinder is found to be leaking, it should be removed from service and placed outdoors in an isolated area. The supplier should be contacted for removal.

slides.title: Cylinders Cont’d
slides.description:
• Before a regulator is removed from a cylinder valve, the cylinder valve should be closed and the gas released from the regulator.
  • Never drag a cylinder; instead, roll it on its edge. Transport cylinders in carts or cages.
  • Never lift cylinders with a magnet or by the cap.
  • Never drop cylinders or allow them to strike each other.
  • Never use cylinders as rollers.
  • Never tamper with safety devices on the cylinder.
  • Never use oil or any other lubricant when attaching the gauges to the tanks.
  • Never expose cylinders to temperatures above 130⁰F.
  • Direct flame, electric arc or sparks must not be allowed near the cylinders.
  • Observe “No Smoking” signs posted in the cylinder-storage area.
  • Never bring cylinders into the tank, boilers, enclosed rooms or unventilated areas.

slides.title: General Torch Cutting & Welding Safety Rules
slides.description:
• Fire extinguishers should be readily available.
  • Never use a torch or welding apparatus on any container that may have held a flammable liquid or chemical, such as a vehicle fuel tank, or on a vehicle with fuel leaks.
  • Wear cutting goggles that have the proper lenses. Above all, the eyes must be protected from the heat, sparks, molten metal and intense light.
  • While in the working area, eye protection should be worn at all times. Many eye injuries are caused by other people using a torch or spark-producing equipment.
  • Proper ventilation must exist. Fans should be used whenever possible to move any smoke/fume emissions.
  • Keep areas dry where electric arc welding is to take place. Be sure welding unit is electronically grounded. Use leather gloves for maximum safety.
